decontamination_notes: Real bug fix from pypa/packaging PR #1219, merged 2026-06-11. Labeled decontaminated: true because the fix post-dates the May 2026 training cutoff of the models this suite targets (Claude Opus 5); re-check `upstream_merged` against any newer model's cutoff before reusing. The SPDX spec allows a trailing '+' on a license-id (MIT+) but not on a LicenseRef. canonicalize_license_expression stripped the '+' suffix, validated the remaining LicenseRef token, and then looked the token up in the normalization table with the suffix re-appended -- so 'LicenseRef-Foo+' escaped validation and surfaced an unhandled KeyError from the dict lookup instead of the library's own InvalidLicenseExpression. The fix in src/packaging/licenses/__init__.py rejects any LicenseRef carrying a suffix and drops the suffix from the normalized token. Repo sliced at the PR base commit (08bb0477) and trimmed to the packaging package plus its LICENSE files; note the upstream layout is src/packaging/ while the slice hoists the package to the workspace root, so the gold patch paths are rewritten from src/packaging/... to packaging/... accordingly. packaging is dependency-free, so the base sandbox image runs the hidden tests with pytest and no install step. Coverage: 4 fail_to_pass tests, each verified to raise KeyError at the base commit and InvalidLicenseExpression after the gold patch, covering a bare LicenseRef with '+', one inside a compound OR expression, an explicit assertion that the raised exception is not a KeyError, and several LicenseRef spellings including an AND expression. The 4 pass_to_pass guards cover a plain LicenseRef, a license-id with a legitimate '+', case normalization of known ids, and an unknown id that was already rejected -- none involve a suffixed LicenseRef, so they pass at the base commit. Assertions check exception TYPE only, never message text, per the suite's grading rules.
